name: CaseFlow
adaptations: Python-only stratum (permitted by docs/protocol.md 'Common public environment'): the TypeScript browser interface becomes server-rendered HTML pages served by the same process at documented paths; hidden tests only check that those pages answer 200 (or 404/401) and contain the relevant data. Behaviour is asserted through the JSON API. There is no Node toolchain in the seed.

Every request keeps the spec.md user prompt verbatim after a '# Request N — <title>' line; precision is added only in a '## What I need' public contract (endpoints, JSON shapes, status and error codes, fixture protocols, clock rules). The seed README carries the protocol's common technical envelope verbatim and the ci.json selector contract.

The seed has exactly ChronoWeave's dependency set and lock (fastapi, uvicorn, httpx; dev pytest, pytest-cov, ruff). FastAPI form parsing (python-multipart) is therefore unavailable: uploads are raw request bodies (CSV) or JSON with base64 (PDF), and pages must parse url-encoded forms themselves.

Seed ci.json is a full-suite selector that prints nothing for Markdown/docs-only changes and ALL otherwise (so it already satisfies the docs-only rule); ci_from_step is 3, the first request with durable background work.

Identity and clock fixture: fixed local sessions are an X-User header ([a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}); before request 6 there is no identity. The controllable clock (GET/PUT/DELETE /api/clock, persisted, frozen when set) is introduced in request 2 because ParcelBox Retry-After waits run on it; all later time-based rules (BoxLoop polling every 5 clock seconds, NoticeSink retries 60 clock seconds after a failure, decided_at, version created_at) use it, so no hidden test waits on wall-clock schedules (only bounded 'within 2 seconds' reactions).
Request 0: blank case name -> 422 name_required, blank document title -> 422 title_required (the prompt's 'title' is applied to documents; cases need a name).

Request 1: manual-file external ids are scoped to a case, not to 'source and workspace' as the fixture table says (workspaces only appear at request 6, and workspace scope would make an identical row in a second case a silent no-op). Row outcome rules (wrong_field_count, external_id_required, title_required, conflicting_duplicate, unchanged) and row numbering are published.

Request 2: imports are background jobs from the start (202 + job resource) because waiting on 429 must not block; 401 marks the connection 'unauthorized' and further imports are refused with 409 credentials_rejected without contacting ParcelBox until credentials change; any other failure fails the job with upstream_error. A changed revision updates the document in place (versions are kept only from request 11).

Request 3: background work runs inside the single service process (no separate worker command); 'restart' is a process restart, which hidden tests perform with SIGTERM while a hub request is held open. Resume semantics are explicit: continue after the last fully saved page, never re-request a saved page; cancel finishes the in-flight request and saves its documents.

Request 4: 'small text PDFs' is defined as a published PDF subset (objects found by scanning, page tree order, Tj/TJ/' operators, literal and hex strings decoded as Latin-1, FlateDecode only, normalisation rule) with a base64 sample pack inside the request; outcomes are imported/unsupported/corrupt per file. No PDF library is available offline.
Request 5: 'ignoring capitals' is Python str.casefold() substring matching; snippets are exact substrings of at most 120 characters containing the first text match.

Request 6: roles owner/editor/viewer with a published matrix; non-members get 404 for everything in a workspace, members lacking the role get 403. Document edits (PATCH) and the integer document 'version' are introduced here because 'editors can change documents' and request 7 reviews a specific version. Pre-existing cases migrate to workspace 'default' owned by 'admin' (not tested: hidden tests use fresh data).
Request 7: decisions must name the version reviewed (409 stale_version otherwise); review_status is the latest decision on the current version.

Request 8: the default responsible person for imported documents is the user who started the import that first created them ('set up its import'). NoticeSink contract: 202 accepted, 200 duplicate, 503 retry, 400 give up (failed), dropped connection after acceptance = retry with the same message_id; notices are observable through GET /api/documents/{id}/notices.
Request 9: inclusive-start/exclusive-end dates as YYYY-MM-DD on UTC midnight; workspace totals for every workspace of the caller (or one workspace_id).

Request 10: BoxLoop polling cadence is defined on the CaseFlow clock; 'show progress while it's preparing' is job stage 'preparing'. After request 13 the source-agnostic hidden checks of requests 6-12 switch from ParcelBox to BoxLoop.
Request 12: the 'example format' is published in the request (format caseflow-case/1) and checked for exact key sets and values equal to the API's own views.

Request 13: retirement is checked as an upgrade: the hidden test extracts the candidate's own previous release (the git commit whose message is exactly 'Request 13', as the runner commits it), runs it on a data directory with finished and unfinished ParcelBox jobs, then starts the current code on that directory. Saved ParcelBox connections report status 'retired' and refuse imports/credential changes with 409 source_retired; new ones get 422 unsupported_source. Earlier ParcelBox-only hidden checks become retirement checks from step 13 (requested removal is not a regression).

Request 14: 'the supplied font files' are two small synthetic .woff2 files given as base64 in the request; hidden tests check byte-exact local serving, @font-face markup, absence of external URLs and a <button id=text-size-toggle aria-pressed> with localStorage persistence in the page source. Rendering, real keyboard interaction and persistence across browser sessions are not exercised.

Request 15: restricted_editor is a new workspace role; 'messages' covers both the notices endpoint and NoticeSink delivery, where a pending message is re-checked before every attempt and cancelled (status 'cancelled') when the recipient can no longer see the document (removed, or a restricted editor no longer responsible).

Not implemented in this version: release rehearsal, artifact counts and independent-deployment measures (request 14's 'release this screen change while the server and imports keep running'), and the spec's CI selection-challenge mutations; they remain operator measures outside the hidden tests.

Probes are applied to a step-15 snapshot as probes/p1..p4 (sorted order maps to hidden/probe_1..probe_4). C1/C2: ArchiveTap uses records/next_page/page with X-Archive-Account/X-Archive-Secret headers and record_key/heading/content/edition fields; C2 adds ordered withdrawal events, a 'withdrawn' flag, owner-only access to withdrawn documents and ?include_withdrawn=true for owners. C3 cannot use an implementation-specific injected fault (the runner applies no per-candidate patch), so the qualified fault is environmental: BoxLoop forgets exports on its own restart (404 on status/download), which the published step-10 contract turns into a job failure; the probe asks for a fresh export instead. C4 removes the export endpoint; earlier export checks detect probe 4 from DRIFT_PROBE=4 or docs/requests/probe-p4-*.md in the candidate and turn into 404 checks.
